why: Each locale's bundle, as `crates/sdk/build.rs` compiles it from `i18n/` into every artefact, in bytes. `crates/intl/tests/pack_budgets.rs` holds each both ways: a bundle over its budget fails, and so does a budget more than a quarter over its bundle, a locale with no budget and a budget with no locale. A budget moves by hand, in the change that needs it, with the reason in the commit. Set 2026-10-23 about a tenth over the bundles measured then: en-Latn 107,795, hi-Deva-IN 70,714, ne-Deva-NP 143,491, sa-Deva 50,528, sa-Latn 39,702. Raised 2026-10-31 for hi-Deva-IN and sa-Deva, which gained the whole of `sdk.calendar` (SR-75). Raised 2026-11-02 for en-Latn and ne-Deva-NP, about a tenth over 121,709 and 163,005, after the lexicon, the chart disagreements, the paya, the doshas and the Jain calendar named their keys (SR-41, SR-32, SR-48, SR-59). Raised 2026-11-03 for hi-Deva-IN, about a tenth over 89,696, after the mundane kinds named their keys (SR-45). Raised 2026-11-10 for hi-Deva-IN, sa-Deva and sa-Latn, about a tenth over 127,163, 96,364 and 75,565, after the three gained the composed text as drafts, `sa-Latn` by derivation (SR-38). Set again 2026-11-10 for every locale, about a tenth over the bundles measured once batch s folded every member's name (SR-12), the Nepali charts' names (SR-36), Kerala's holidays (SR-03), the printed abbreviations (SR-85) and the month-and-year patterns (SR-86): en-Latn 168,596, hi-Deva-IN 183,950, ne-Deva-NP 228,697, sa-Deva 140,118, sa-Latn 108,920. Raised 2026-11-10 for sa-Deva and sa-Latn, about a tenth over 207,036 and 156,432, after every festival was named in Sanskrit. Set again 2026-11-14 for every locale, about a tenth over the bundles measured once Uttar Pradesh's and Odisha's holidays (SR-03) and 28 civil days of the consumer's list (SR-01) were named: en-Latn 183,669, hi-Deva-IN 206,678, ne-Deva-NP 251,562, sa-Deva 229,930, sa-Latn 172,022. Set again 2026-11-15 for every locale, about a tenth over the bundles measured once the rashifal's areas, colours, verdicts and bands were named (SR-124): en-Latn 198,448, hi-Deva-IN 229,002, ne-Deva-NP 273,723, sa-Deva 251,985, sa-Latn 186,911. Raised 2026-11-17 for hi-Deva-IN, about a tenth over 251,580, the SR-124 bundle with the SR-123 gazette names' 22,578 bytes beside it. Set again 2026-11-17 for every locale when SR-110's effect notes joined SR-123's and SR-124's names in one batch: about a tenth over each bundle the three measured, summed (SR-110 added 25,530, 42,600, 40,293, 43,376 and 27,500 bytes in the order above). Raised 2026-11-17 for hi-Deva-IN, sa-Deva and sa-Latn when SR-128's Hindi festival names and text terms joined the same batch: about a tenth over the summed bundles (SR-128 added 69,474, 34,434 and 24,992 bytes). Lowered 2026-11-22 for hi-Deva-IN to 335,000, since the summed estimate of 400,000 stood more than a quarter over the 307,207 bytes the batch measured on CI, and 335,000 also holds the intl words lane to come. Set 2026-11-17 for en-Latn-NP, Nepal's English, a tenth over its 495 bytes: its metadata alone, every word falling back to en-Latn (SR-140). Raised 2026-11-23 for en-Latn-NP to 2,200, estimated from its sources and held within a quarter of its bundle by the test, once it named the twelve signs as Nepal's English press does (SR-151, C2332). Raised 2026-11-23 for hi-Deva-IN to 373,000, about a tenth over the 338,795 bytes measured once SR-145's sixteen more international days were named (C2346); the thirty Newar, Tharu and vrata days that joined them in batch rc.9 (C2347 to C2358) measured 338,744 bytes on the same base alone, and 373,000 holds the two together within a quarter. Raised 2026-11-24 for en-Latn and ne-Deva-NP to 290,000 and 405,000, over the 254,894 and 361,682 bytes measured on CI once the rashifal's reading voice joined them (SR-152), and holding the muhurta reasons to come (SR-154).
